golden_baseline_location: parent-run deterministic legacy chain (NS=demo, TP_FAKETIME=2026-01-15, RUN_ALL_SLEEP=0): end-state after run_all.sh = 2 archived .dat files, 100 silver-equivalent parsed rows, 6 golden report aggregate rows; manifest at parent path tp-golden/databricks-20260816T175547Z/SHA256SUMS

acceptance_checks.description: ow_tp_custbill_estate is a single Databricks multi-task job wiring ingest -> parse -> finance via task dependencies — no sleep-based sequencing anywhere.
max_concurrent_runs=1 on the estate job so overlapping schedules cannot interleave (retires the crontab overlap deficiency).
One estate run from a clean ns slice reproduces the full golden end-state: registered raw files, 100 silver rows, six cent-exact gold aggregates.
A failing task fails the run visibly (downstream tasks skipped, run result FAILED) — no blanket 2>/dev/null || true suppression; estate_run_log records per-task outcome.

planted_anomalies.description: Parent triggers an estate run against a deliberately trailer-mismatched drop; the parse task must fail/quarantine and the run log must show the estate run attributing it — never a green run over partial data.

planted_anomalies.reason: Provoking two genuinely concurrent scheduled runs in the shared workspace within the demo window is not reliably reproducible; max_concurrent_runs=1 is asserted from the job definition instead.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Orchestration moves no data itself; it must not introduce any decoding layer between tasks — each task's own contract governs its bytes.

malformed_record_policy.details: The estate run log must never record a task as succeeded with NULL/missing outcome fields; unknown task state is a run failure, not a plausible-looking success row.

empty_input_semantics.details: An estate run over an empty landing slice completes with all tasks no-op successful and prior outputs untouched (legacy: run_all.sh over an empty drop exits 0 having changed nothing).
